title: Animal and plant cell
description: Tap the nucleus in an animal cell. The kind param also draws a plant cell, with a wall, chloroplasts, and a large vacuole.
prerequisites: Living things are made of cells
learningObjectives: Identify the nucleus in an animal cell or a plant cell
Explain how a plant cell differs from an animal cell

params.description: Which cell to draw: animal or plant.

events.name: organelle_selected
events.description: The child selected an organelle in the cell.

events.name: cell_labeled
events.description: The child labeled the nucleus of this cell.

tutorGuide.intro: This cell drawing changes with the kind param. Animal is the start. Plant adds the wall, chloroplasts, and a large vacuole.
steps: Look at the shape of the cell.
Name one part a plant cell has that this animal cell does not.
observationPrompts: What shape is the outside of this cell?
Which parts show up only when the cell is a plant cell?

misconceptions.belief: Plant cells and animal cells have the same parts.
misconceptions.response: A plant cell has a cell wall, chloroplasts, and a large vacuole. An animal cell does not.

misconceptions.belief: The cell wall and the nucleus are the same part.
misconceptions.response: The wall is the stiff outer layer of a plant cell. The nucleus sits inside and holds the cell's instructions.

hints: The nucleus is the round purple part.
A plant cell is more like a box, with a thick wall.
Look for green chloroplasts only on the plant cell.

successCriteria.description: Labeled the nucleus of the cell

accessibility.screenReaderSummary: A cell diagram. Tap the nucleus to label it. A plant cell adds a wall, chloroplasts, and a large vacuole.
